vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: hugging-face-cli
Version: 1.0.6

The skill provides a comprehensive interface for the Hugging Face CLI, including high-risk operations like repository deletion, cloud job execution (hf jobs run), and endpoint management. A significant security concern is the recommended installation method via 'curl | bash' (https://hf.co/cli/install.sh) in SKILL.md, which is a common vector for remote code execution. While the skill includes safety rules and confirmation requirements for destructive actions, the combination of broad account access and the shell-based installation script warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose: it expects the hf CLI and a Hugging Face token (HF_TOKEN) and only describes hf commands; no unrelated credentials or file-system access are requested.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Hugging Face CLI) match the declared requirements (hf binary) and primaryEnv (HF_TOKEN). The env var and binary are exactly what you'd expect for controlling the Hugging Face Hub.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md focuses on running the hf CLI and provides examples for download/upload/repos/jobs/endpoints. It does not instruct reading unrelated system files or environment variables beyond HF_TOKEN. The examples imply access to local files when uploading, which is inherent to the CLI's purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec in the registry; the docs recommend installing via curl -LsSf https://hf.co/cli/install.sh | bash. That URL is an official Hugging Face domain, but curl|bash executes a remote script and is a moderate operational risk—users should review the installer before running it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only HF_TOKEN is required and is declared as the primary credential. This is proportionate. Important: write-scoped tokens permit destructive actions (create/delete repos, upload, delete buckets); prefer read-scoped tokens for exploratory tasks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not forced-always and is user-invocable. It does not request persistent system-wide privileges or to modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default on the platform but is not itself a red flag here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be what it says: it uses the official hf CLI and needs HF_TOKEN. Before installing/using:
- Prefer creating a minimal-permission HF token (Read only) unless you need uploads/deletes. Write tokens enable destructive actions.
- If you must install the CLI, review the installer script at https://hf.co/cli/install.sh before running curl | bash.
- Be aware that any command the agent runs with this skill could access local files (e.g., hf upload) if given paths — avoid granting the skill access to sensitive local files.
- If you grant a write-scoped token temporarily, consider revoking it or rotating it afterwards.
- If you want extra safety, keep this skill user-invocable only (do not allow it to run autonomously) so you approve actions that modify remote repos, buckets, or endpoints.
